From Earthbound satellite receivers - to state-of-the-art nanosatellites and autonomous lunar robots, researchers at SnT infuse Luxembourg's vibrant space industry with new perspectives and innovative solutions. In addition to long-term, high-risk research, SnT engages in demand driven collaborative projects with industry and the public sector. Therefore, the centre has set up a partnership program with now over 55 members, where it develops strategic areas addressing challenges confronting the industry and the public sector in ICT. These resulting concepts present a genuine, long-lasting competitive advantage for companies in Luxembourg and beyond.

entityDescription:
GAIKER, member of Basque Research and Technology Alliance, BRTA, is a Technology Centre devoted to the technological innovation. From its beginnings in 1985, it uptakes, develops and transfers technology to the industry.
GAIKER has carried out close to 567 projects and has leaded or taken part in 132 European Projects framed in Programmes of the Europe acting as partner to gather new advance knowledge for further industrial application. GAIKER’s activity is focused on the transfer to its customers of the technology and the know-how acquired during the up-taking process. From its foundation, the Centre has carried out close to 1,550 R&D projects “under contract” for customers coming from a wide range of sectors (Pharmaceutical Industry, Chemical Industry, Human and Animal Health, Engineering and Consultancy Firms, Public Administrations, Automotive Industries, Construction, Packing and Packaging and Home Appliances, amongst others). This wide offer is possible thanks to its highly qualified staff; nowadays 95 employees. Furthermore, the 8,750 m2of premises -located in the Technological Park of Bizkaia (Zamudio)- include an extensive network of laboratories, as well as pilot plants where processes are optimised, and prototypes developed. GAIKER is a Centre of Innovation dedicated to offer quality solutions to the technological needs of its customers. The certification of its R&D&i Management System in accordance with UNE 166002:2014 standard in 2019.
· In the BIOTECHNOLOGY Area, the Centre carries out in vitro and ex vivo preclinical studies aimed at the toxicological, pharmacokinetic and functional evaluation of compounds (including active ingredients, drugs, cosmetics, functional ingredients and nanocomposites), for which it has the GLP (Good Laboratory Practice) Certificate of Compliance. It is also an expert in the development of biodetection systems of biological targets for applications in human, animal, plant or environmental health. It works in industrial biotechnology focused on improving industrial processes through the selection and production of microorganisms and/or enzymes.
· In the SUSTAINABLE COMPOSITES AND FUNCTIONAL POLYMERS' Area, the Centre develop more sustainable polymeric materials with better functional and structural performance addressing the entire life cycle of the product: from its design and processing to its recycling and reuse. We formulate thermoplastics/thermosets by incorporating bio-based, recycled and biodegradable materials in their conception to adjust their properties to the product/process and optimize their processing conditions in pilot plants as well as their sustainability.
In the same way, the area works on extending the potential of additive manufacturing to new range of materials and functionalities. We either make the materials have sensor performance, or incorporate sensors in the product and the process, to bolster the concept of “Industry 4.0” from the materials' technology perspective. We functionalise the materials to give them new performance with respect to their electrical and durability properties (anti-scratch, self-repairing, fungicide, ...) and develop films and active packaging. 
GAIKER is deeply involved in Recycling and Circular Economy: on the characterisation and treatment of post-consumer waste flow from every origin as well as industrial scraps, using innovative identification and separation systems; We develop ad-hoc chemical recycling processes to obtain monomers, chemical blocks, and fuels derived from plastic waste.

description:
The Centre for Innovation in Polymer Engineering (PIEP) is a private non-profit association, of a technological and scientific matrix, with a business management model.
Founded on December 13, 2000, at the initiative of the industry and in collaboration with the Department of Polymer Engineering at the University of Minho (DEP-UM) and the Support Institute for Small and Medium Enterprises and Innovation (IAPMEI), PIEP intends to provide an excellent response in the delivery of products and services promptly, oriented to the R&D+i needs of companies in the plastics and related sectors, through innovation activities, technology transfer, technical-scientific consultancy, and service provision.
In general, PIEP acts in terms of the provision of testing and testing services and failure diagnoses, the development of new materials and products, processing technologies, and productive tools, based on the promotion of the principles of sustainable development (Circular Economy and Environment). 
PIEP also contributes to training, supporting the development of human resources with capacity and experience in industrial innovation in the field of polymer engineering.
entityDescription:
CENTRE FOR INNOVATION IN POLYMER ENGINEERING

PIEP is a private non-profit research and development organisation providing consultancy, materials, product and processing technology development, as well as testing services for the polymer industry worldwide and related sectors.

Established in 2001 by some of the leading national plastic companies, UMinho and with the national government support through IAPMEI, PIEP holds a wide range of associated members, the majority of plastic industry affiliates (plastics converters, machinery suppliers, mould making companies, compounders, and material suppliers). Based in Guimarães (Portugal) and strategically located in UMinho Campus, close to the Polymer Engineering Department (DEP), PIEP currently employs over 30 people with relevant academic background and applied R&D experience in a wide range of polymer science and engineering domains.

Its 3,000sq meter state-of-the-art facilities (an investment over 6.5 million Euros from private and public sector) provides extensive capabilities for polymer characterisation and testing (mechanical, thermal, rheological, chemical and thermo-physical), thermoplastic materials development and processing (conventional and multi-material injection moulding, single and twin screw extrusion, co-extrusion, blow moulding, thermoforming), thermoset materials processing (vacuum infusion, RTM) and advanced computational modelling tools for product and process design and engineering.

Commitment to industry: PIEP, in cooperation with the academic staff from the Polymer Engineering Department of UMinho, provides research with up to date scientific knowledge, ensuring the best and innovative problem-solving approaches to industry’s innovation challenges and needs.

Our mission: To be a Polymer Engineering Innovation Center, with a regional, national and international scope that efficiently formalizes the link between the industry and the University, capable to respond, on time, the R&D companies needs (in the case of SMEs, even constituting their valence in this field), promoting and supporting the human resources training with experience in industrial innovation activities, aimed to convert ideas into products.

Our Vision: To be a reference partner in applied research, development, and innovation for the polymers and composites industry at the national and international level, promoting the materialisation of new ideas and concepts that serve as a basis for sustainable economic development and industrial competitiveness.

Relevant skills/experience: With its core knowledge and competencies based on materials science – engineering - processing technologies - testing, PIEP is actively engaged in the development of research projects, bringing together a set of integrated and interconnected capabilities that serve the fundamental purpose of its existence: to support the national and international industry in the development of materials, engineering, production technologies and tests applied to polymer materials, products, and systems.

The Telecom-network R&D Team has been working in the network development and satellite systems for more than 15 years for industrial and R&D purposes. It has recognized skills in the satellite telecommunication area through collaboration with French Spatial Agency (CNES), Marlink (Leading satellite operator for maritime market), Airbus Defense & Space or Thales Alenia Space.

Since 2009, the R&D team is the official maintainer of the open-source satellite emulator OpenSAND, as well as the creator and main contributor of the open-source metrology tool OpenBACH since 2016. Since 2018, the team is the main developer of the Satellite-NS3 (SNS3) open-source simulator.

Since 2007 Viveris has carried out more than 30 R&T projects funded by the French spatial agency (CNES), and in collaboration with academic and industrial partners. Most of project deal with SATCOM (GEO/LEO) and hybrid systems (terrestrial),and in particular the performance evaluation of services/applications in these networks and the optimisations at different levels (access, network, transport and service). Some of the topics addressed during these projects are listed herein: hybrid ADSL/Satellite/cellular/IoT network architectures, IPTV, evaluation of TCP and new transport protocols (QUIC/HTTP3) on SATCOM, evaluation of PEP proxies, CDNs caching, traffic engineering and load balancing (including MPTCP), FEC performances, ROHC header compression, DPI and Machine Learning techniques applied to satellite networks and SDN/NFV Virtualization.

entityDescription:
Neptune is an innovative SME established in 2014, founded by a team of experts in water loss, satellite image analysis, data transmission and remote sensing applications. Water leakage is a paramount worldwide problem because the subsoil pipelines are old and lose an average between 30 to 40% of potable water, with a peak up to 60%. Our idea is to enhance the water loss research system with a "disruptive technology" using EO data to analyse the soil moisture content (SMC) to identify small and big water leaks. Actual trends, analysed by the European Environment Agency (source https://www.eea.europa.eu/) shows the world water consumption doubles every 20 years, more than twice as fast as population growth with the risk in the future that part of the citizens will not have access to drinking water. Saving water resources through the timely identification of leaks is fundamental for users to have guaranteed supply of drinking water, but it is also important for operators in order to lower their operating costs and guarantees of service.
Neptune’s team was looking for a new space-derived technology to apply to daily water leaks issues, with a TTP (Technology Transfer Project), from space technologies to terrestrial applications. Research and a passion for space have led to the identification of the possibility of monitoring soil moisture through the analysis of L-band SAR satellite images, which due to its wavelength is able to penetrate the ground.
The idea, born in 2014, is to innovate the water loss research system with a "disruptive technology" and not by simply improving existing techniques. The main issue that we wanted to address is the amount of water purified and lost during the network source to users. To solve this problem, each year players in the industry issue contracts for millions of Euros for leakage research. The detection service is paid by the kilometre checked and, normally, with the existing technology, a team composed of 2 people can only assess 5 km of water network each day. With NE.P.T.UN.E. Water Leaks Sat (Satellite Network Project To Uncover Extended Water Leaks) we can increase the daily km checked from 5 to 30 because operators are able to go directly to POIs (points of interest) generated by processing satellite images. This way, we can check in 1 day what other competitors check in 1 week, with a great decrease in costs.

entityName: University of Ljubljana, Faculty of Computer and Information Science
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Computer and Information Science of the University of Ljubljana is Slovenia’s leading educational and research institution for computer and information science.
The Faculty’s main function is educating undergraduate and graduate computer science experts of various profiles, as well as engaging in research work which generates new knowledge and uncovers solutions to contemporary problems. The Faculty also offers additional educational activities in computer and information science for several professional profiles by hosting lectures and workshops to increase the level of computer literacy in the country. Its public events also serve to popularise ideas about computers, especially among young people.
The Faculty was founded in 1996, when the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science split into two separate faculties. The study of computer science itself began at the University of Ljubljana back in 1973, first as an elective programme after the 2nd year of electrical engineering study, and has been an independent study programme since 1982. In 2014, the Faculty moved to a new building in Brdo at the outskirts of Ljubljana.
The Faculty is a full member of theUniversity of Ljubljana. The University was founded in 1919 and is the oldest and largest higher education and scientific research institution in Slovenia.
